title: Shipped default witness configuration
statement: Ship a default the project neither operates nor overloads: an RFC 3161 timestamp authority for the per-batch countersignature and clock, plus a trust-minimised roll-up anchor on a slow interval. A transparency log such as Rekor is opt-in — for operators self-hosting one, or whose volume suits a public instance — and never the shipped default, because a 10-second cadence against a public good is not acceptable use.
source: Independence — the shipped default anchors to a log we do not run
verify: The canonical default-config.yaml is read by the test, so the shipped default cannot drift from what is asserted; defaultWitnessWarning() states that it does NOT close classes 4 and 5
evidence: packages/witnesses; TSA plus OpenTimestamps roll-up, Rekor commented out with FR-47's reason

title: Documented CLI contract
statement: Provide the entry points and flags printed in Getting started: collect-oma, mcp-proxy (--upstream, --out), verify (--policy), coverage (--from, --to) and disclose (--event, --out).
verify: CLI contract test executes every documented invocation verbatim

title: Witness publishes signed tree heads
statement: The witness publishes its own signed tree head so an operator or third party can detect a rolled-back or equivocating witness.
source: Durability — losing a witness must not lose the evidence
verify: The witness publishes its own signed tree head; detectRollback compares two observed heads and says which contradicts which
evidence: StatefulWitness.treeHead + client.detectRollback; the earlier head must have been RETAINED by whoever polled it, which the module says

title: Witness key rotation
statement: Rotate witness keys while keeping historical countersignatures verifiable, by publishing a signed key history.
verify: A retired witness key still verifies, against a published key history that is VALIDATED first: the note must exist, verify under a key that is itself in the list, and sign a digest that covers the list as presented. A key absent from a valid history is inconclusive, not a failure
evidence: validateKeyHistory() in packages/verify/src/verify.mjs; without the digest check a key could be appended after signing and the signature would still check out

title: Build provenance attestation
statement: Publish a provenance attestation for every released collector artifact, binding the digest to its source commit and build, so the digest in a heartbeat can be independently traced.
source: Provenance — a build digest you can check
verify: Attestation verifies against the published artifact and source revision
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml — actions/attest-build-provenance over every tarball, plus npm provenance

title: Signed releases and SBOM
statement: Sign every release and publish an SBOM with pinned dependencies.
source: Provenance — signed releases and an SBOM
verify: Signature and SBOM present and verified in CI for each release
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml — npm publish --provenance and a CycloneDX SBOM with pinned dependencies

title: Key compromise recovery
statement: Document and support recovery from operator key compromise: a declared, countersigned discontinuity rather than a silent re-key.
verify: A `discontinuity` record kind naming the last sound epoch, the new root key and a required reason; reported prominently as DISCONTINUITY, never bridged — no affirmative signing claim spans it and the report says the reader must re-pin out of band. The declaration is signed by the key it disowns and the report says so
evidence: record.mjs allowlist + Collector.declareDiscontinuity + verify.mjs; DES-06 called it a policy record, which the per-kind allowlist cannot express — a distinct kind also lets the verifier find discontinuities BY KIND, which is what makes 'never silently bridged' checkable

title: Witness time source
statement: The witness clock derives from a documented, traceable time source, and the verifier surfaces the witness's declared time discipline.
source: Durability — the clock the witness stamps with
verify: Every witness type declares its time discipline, including that OpenTimestamps is not a clock at all and a TSA's clock is disciplined as its practice statement says and no better
evidence: TIME_DISCIPLINE in packages/witnesses

title: Witness store durability
statement: The witness store is replicated and recoverable, with a documented recovery point objective, because a witness that loses its roots destroys the corroboration it exists to provide.
source: Durability — losing a witness must not lose the evidence
verify: A runnable drill (`npm run drill:restore`) rather than a described procedure: it takes a backup, advances past it, destroys the live store, restores, and asserts the restored witness refuses both a conflicting submission AND the operator's honest next one — then recovers by resubmitting from the height the witness reports. It exits non-zero if it measures no loss, so it cannot pass without exercising a stale backup
evidence: packages/witness-self/drill/restore.mjs + docs/witness-restore-drill.md; RPO is one submission for a crash and the backup interval for a restore, measured rather than assumed. Replication is stated as a deployment concern this project specifies and does not implement

title: No agent code changes
statement: Both collectors integrate by dependency and configuration only; no change to the customer's agent code is required.
source: Why — without asking you to change your agent code
verify: Byte-identical agent source before and after integration, for both collectors
evidence: packages/collect-oma/test/integration.test.mjs hashes the agent source before and after integration and asserts the run outcome is unchanged; the agent fixture mentions Splitstick nowhere

title: WPS states the time discipline
statement: The practice statement names the witness's time source and the limits of the time assertion.
source: Witness Practice Statement — per its clock
verify: §4 names each witness type's time source and the limits of the time assertion, including that OpenTimestamps is not a clock at all and that none of them establishes when an action OCCURRED — only when a root was received, and only from above
evidence: lint-practice-statement.mjs pairs it with TIME_DISCIPLINE in packages/witnesses

title: Bounty: cash deferred until funded
statement: State publicly that a cash award opens only if the project is funded, rather than promising money that is not held.
verify: Terms published with the condition stated; no figure advertised as available

title: Accept third-party attack classes
statement: Accept contributed attack classes by pull request, with attribution. A goal, explicitly not a launch gate.
source: Attack class section — the suite is open, contributions are invited
verify: Contribution path documented; not referenced in any release gate

title: No fail-closed option
statement: MUST NOT provide any configuration, flag or build that makes the collector block an agent run. Fail-open is a design constraint, not a setting.
source: Operations — a design constraint, not a setting
verify: Config schema review; no enforcement path exists; rejected as a feature request by policy

title: State the resourcing honestly
statement: Publish that the project is unfunded and what that means: no hosted witness, no accreditation, no certification mark, and recognition rather than cash. Stated plainly rather than implied by omission.
verify: Section present in the release notes and the README
evidence: Resourcing section in README and notes

title: Canonicalisation completeness
statement: The canonical encoding must cover every field of the action record at every nesting depth. A test must prove that mutating any single field, at any depth, changes the leaf digest.
source: Capture — action record: tool name, arguments, result, approval decision
verify: Property test mutating each field in turn, including nested argument keys; every mutation must change the digest
evidence: spec/vectors/jcs.json; leafPaths property test in record.test.mjs; leaf-level mutation test in leaf.test.mjs

title: Roll-up anchoring
statement: Anchor a periodic summary checkpoint covering many batches, separately from the per-batch soft anchor, so a public or rate-limited witness receives a handful of entries per day rather than thousands.
verify: A roll-up commits to the CHECKPOINT NOTES; a single batch is provable under it by an ordinary inclusion proof, and successive roll-ups are prefixes of each other
evidence: Collector.rollup + Anchorer.anchorRollup + verifyRollups; kept in their own directory because a roll-up read as a checkpoint is a false TREE_MISMATCH

title: Cross-pack consistency verification
statement: Given two or more evidence packs, detect a record inconsistent with a checkpoint already countersigned in an earlier pack — so a record truncated below a height previously disclosed is contradicted offline, with no live service.
verify: A pack disclosed earlier holding a countersigned height above where this record ends emits TRUNCATED_BELOW_DISCLOSED; a differing root at the same height is reported as a fork with neither preferred
evidence: verifyStore opts.disclosed

title: Counterparty reference capture
statement: Extract externally issued identifiers from a tool result and index them for reconciliation. The index lives in the deletable content store, never in the chain, because a transaction reference can itself be identifying.
verify: A result containing an external reference is indexed and queryable; the index is removed by crypto-shredding
evidence: extractRefs + the deletable reference index in content.mjs; shredded with the content

title: Resist truncation below a disclosed height
statement: A record truncated below a sequence already disclosed in a countersigned pack must be detectable by comparing the two, without any stateful witness.
verify: TRUNCATED_BELOW_DISCLOSED emitted from a height a counterparty already holds
evidence: verifyStore opts.disclosed + spec/failure-codes.json

title: Reconciliation guidance
statement: Document reconciliation against counterparty records as a detection method for erasure and omission, with its limits stated: it requires access to the counterparty and it is a procedure an auditor performs, not a guarantee the software makes.
verify: docs/reconciliation.md states the procedure and five limits: it needs access to the counterparty, it is a procedure with a procedure's failure modes, its coverage is bounded by the counterparty's completeness, it is retrospective, and it does not establish WHEN
evidence: docs/reconciliation.md, with the preference order putting it last because it is the most expensive and least verifiable

title: Collector instance identity
statement: Each collector instance has a stable identity that scopes its chain and its log origin. Records carry the run they belong to as a field; the chain itself is collector-scoped, so concurrent runs interleave in one log and heartbeats need no run at all.
verify: Two concurrent runs produce one contiguous chain with correct run tags; a heartbeat emitted with no run active is chained and anchored
evidence: collector-scoped chain in chain.mjs and collector.mjs; interleaved-run test; heartbeat with no run

title: Document the collector-patch limit
statement: State plainly, wherever coverage attestation is described, that a collector patched to report a valid digest while suppressing actions is not detectable without remote attestation, which this release does not provide.
source: Coverage attestation; Threat model — residual risk
verify: Statement present in the threat model, the coverage report output, and DES-10; claims audit checks no surface implies otherwise
evidence: The limit in the threat model, DES-10 and the coverage report's OUTPUT, with tools/lint-claims.mjs checking all three — a limit in a design file is one the person acting on the report never sees. Each half of the check was shown to fail when removed

title: Verifier states witness-set capabilities
statement: The verifier prints what the configured or observed witness set can and cannot establish — in particular whether any witness maintains operator sequence state, and therefore whether truncation above the last disclosed height is detectable at all.
verify: The capability statement is derived from the proofs actually present, not from configuration, and prints quorum per class
evidence: report() in packages/verify/src/verify.mjs

title: Reserved slot for gap declarations
statement: Pre-allocate storage sufficient to write a gap declaration, so the declaration can be written even when the store is otherwise exhausted. If even that fails, the condition is surfaced out of band and the next successful write declares the lost window.
verify: A 64 KiB reserve written when the store is created, never touched by ordinary records, released only to write a gap declaration; its absence afterwards is the signal it was spent. If even that fails the condition is surfaced out of band and the collector degrades
evidence: Store.releaseReserve + Collector.declareGap; the failed append degraded the collector so the retry was refused before reaching the store — the mechanism would have been dead in production

title: Action record and chain entry are separate structures
statement: The canonicalised, hashed ActionRecord is immutable and contains no chain metadata. prev, leaf and head live in a ChainEntry wrapper that is never canonicalised, so the digest of a record can never depend on a value derived from it. Conformance vectors publish the exact bytes hashed.
source: Integrity — chained, salted, ratcheted; Capture — action record
verify: Conformance vectors: given a fixed ActionRecord, the canonical bytes, leaf and head are byte-exact. A test asserts no chain field appears inside the canonicalised subject
evidence: ActionRecord and ChainEntry are separate structures; validateRecord rejects leaf/prev/head/salt in the subject

title: Unknown-loss intervals
statement: When the observation counter did not survive — an unrecoverable crash with the counter only in memory — declare an unknown-loss interval bounded by the last durable checkpoint and the first record after restart. Never fabricate an exact span. The two kinds of loss evidence are distinct record kinds and a verifier reports them differently.
source: Operations — fails open, loudly; Coverage attestation
verify: An unknown-loss interval bounded by the last durable checkpoint and the restart, declared when the counter did not survive; a first run declares nothing, because a first run is not a loss
evidence: Collector.reconcileObservations -> gapUnknown; declaring one would put a permanent unknown-loss interval at the head of every log ever created. The span is measured from what is ACCOUNTED FOR — written records and the spans already declared — so a gap is never re-declared and the interval after a restart starts where the last declaration ended

title: Observation counter durability
statement: Checkpoint the observation counter durably at each batch flush, so an unrecoverable crash loses at most the current window and the unknown-loss interval is bounded rather than open-ended.
verify: The counter is written atomically at each batch flush and reconciled against the chain on open; level means no loss, ahead means an exact span to declare, absent means FR-60's interval. A counter BEHIND the accounted position is the ordinary mid-window state and declares nothing: the counter advances at each flush while source_seq advances at every observation, so behind is what the state between flushes looks like
evidence: Store.writeObservationCounter + Collector.reconcileObservations; resuming from the last WRITTEN source_seq reused the numbers that were spent, so the hole closed up and a lossy run read as complete. Treating a behind counter as tampering was then wrong in the other direction — it refused to open the store after any crash between a reconciliation and the next checkpoint, with hand-editing the counter file as the only way back. A restored-older counter under-declares a loss, which is the operator misreporting their own loss and indistinguishable from the normal state

title: Retries, timeouts and errors in the schema
statement: The record schema represents a failed, timed-out or retried tool call explicitly: an outcome enum, an attempt number, and a correlation id grouping attempts of one logical action. source_seq advances once per observed ATTEMPT, not per logical action, because a timed-out attempt may already have caused an external side effect and must stay independently accountable. Correlation, not the counter, is what groups attempts. The correlation identifier is opaque and randomly generated, never derived from a payload, user or session, because it is retained after erasure.
verify: Interleaved retries across two correlations keep source_seq strictly increasing; an omitted retry is detected as a source_seq gap; coverage reports attempt count and logical-action count separately
evidence: outcome, attempt and correlation in record.mjs; Collector.correlate; unresolved calls settled as timeout

title: Pinned operator identity
statement: The acceptance policy names the operator identity the reader expects, and the verifier reports any pack presented under a different key or origin rather than silently accepting it. Nothing prevents an operator maintaining a second log; the guarantee is that a reader who pinned an identity is told when they are shown another.
verify: A pack under another origin emits IDENTITY_UNPINNED; the right origin with the wrong key is also reported; pinning nothing reads as pinning nothing rather than as a pass
evidence: packages/verify/test/assumptions.test.mjs

title: Collector self-reported configuration attestation
statement: Each heartbeat carries a digest of the capture configuration the collector reports for itself — upstreams proxied, interfaces bound, heartbeat and anchor intervals — so a change to THAT configuration is recorded and visible. It does not detect an execution path created outside the collector: such a path leaves the collector reporting an unchanged digest and nothing diverges. This is provenance of a self-report, not independent observation.
verify: Changing a declared upstream alters the attested digest and emits a policy record; a test asserts that a path bypassing the collector entirely produces NO signal, so the limit is pinned by a test rather than by prose
evidence: capture.mjs captureSurface/captureDigest, attested in every heartbeat; duplicates and unknown keys refused rather than collapsed or ignored, because two different declarations must not produce one digest and a misspelled `upstream:` would attest to a narrower surface than was written. The bypass test is PAIRED: it asserts a path outside the collector produces no signal AND, over the same store, that a declared change produces one — without that half it would pass against a deleted implementation

title: Operator-declared key custody
statement: The key custody class — non-exportable KMS or HSM, versus a software key — is declared in a chained record per epoch, because an HSM signature and a file-key signature are byte-identical and a verifier cannot otherwise tell them apart. The declaration proves the operator declared it, not that the key was non-exportable or later destroyed. Custody is reported as operator-declared unless a provider attestation document is supplied alongside, which is the only path to independently supported custody.
verify: A `custody` record kind, chained; custody_basis admits only 'operator-declared' and the validator refuses 'independently-supported' outright
evidence: record.mjs allowlist + Collector.custody; rotate(next, {declare:true}) means an epoch is never undeclared

title: Compare expected witnesses against proofs present
statement: Each checkpoint records which witnesses were expected for it, given their tier and cadence, and the verifier compares that against the proofs in the pack. A proof that is expected and absent is reported as missing and inconclusive — it may be pending under fail-open, the witness may have been unavailable, or the receipt may have been removed, and the verifier cannot tell which from absence alone. Demonstrating removal requires an earlier pack that contained it, which is cross-pack comparison.
verify: Remove a proof: WITNESS_MISSING is reported as inconclusive, never as deletion. A witness on a slower tier with no proof yet is reported as not-yet-expected. A pack pair where one holds the proof and the later one does not yields removal
evidence: verify.mjs tier-aware expectation; a witness on the roll-up tier is reported not-yet-expected rather than missing, because its proofs live in the roll-up envelopes and a permanent inconclusive on every correctly configured log is how a finding stops being read. Absence is never reported as deletion: pending, unavailable and removed are indistinguishable from absence alone, and demonstrating removal takes FR-54's cross-pack comparison

title: Unwitnessed outage ceiling
statement: Fail-open must not become indefinite. An unwitnessed_ceiling sets the point at which the collector raises an alert out of band, and beyond which the coverage report refuses to issue a completeness claim spanning the outage, stating the unwitnessed window instead.
verify: Past the ceiling an alert is raised OUT OF BAND through a callback that writes no record, once per breach rather than once per flush; the breach clears on drain and `breaches` keeps the window; a ceiling of zero or less is refused at config load
evidence: Anchorer.ceilingBreached/onCeilingBreached + config positive(); an alert about the log's integrity written into that log asks the suspect to carry the complaint. The age was computed from the queued entry's `since`, so a single unparseable `since` on disk made the age NaN and every comparison against the ceiling false — the ceiling that exists to stop fail-open becoming indefinite was itself silenced indefinitely by one corrupt field. Store.readQueue now refuses such an entry, and an unmeasurable age counts as over the ceiling rather than under it

title: Padding is a record kind
statement: A padding leaf is an explicit record kind in the version-1 enum, with its own record_seq, source_seq null, no tool or payload fields, and a random nonce so no two padding records share a leaf. Padding leaves without records would break record_seq equals tree_size.
verify: Two real records plus three padding records yield tree_size 5 and record_seq 5; a verifier counts real and padding records separately; a mixed real-and-padding log verifies end to end

title: Every assurance claim names its evidence
statement: Each assurance claim in the specifications and the release notes names the evidence that supports it, classified as independent, operator-declared, or none. A claim resting only on the operator-controlled collector is worded as an assertion, never as a verified guarantee. This rule exists because the design repeatedly acquired guarantees its own threat model excludes.
verify: Claims audit per release checks each assurance claim against the register; npm run review flags a curated set of overclaim phrasings

title: Validate a provider custody attestation
statement: Before reporting custody as independently supported, validate the attestation: issuer chains to a provider root named in the acceptance policy, document signature valid over the bytes presented, attested key is the one that signed this epoch, attestation period covers the epoch, and the document actually asserts non-exportability. Even all five together do not establish historical key destruction, which remains operator-declared.
verify: All five checks reported separately, each with a test that breaks only it. Check 5 reads YubiHSM 2's own Origin and Capabilities BIT STRINGs at the OIDs Yubico publishes, and requires BOTH that the key was generated on the device (not imported, not imported under wrap) and that it lacks exportable-under-wrap. Fixtures are vendor FORMAT; no real provider document has ever been put through it, and every result carries provider_untested: true
evidence: packages/core/src/attestation.mjs over the shared packages/core/src/trustpath.mjs; an end-entity certificate cannot act as a CA; bit indexing follows Yubico's own reference parser (docs.yubico.com/hardware/oid/oid-product-arc.html, YubicoLabs/yubihsm-parse-attestation); establishes_destruction is hard-coded false with a test asserting it
